transcription: Main article text only (site header and mega-menu, the Spanish toggle, the in-page anchor nav listing the five section links, the 'Search Terms'/'Topics'/'Related Items' blocks, the 'September 2022' date line, the 'Return to top' link and the footer removed). The example phishing email is a page image (not stored); its introducing sentence is kept and the three • 'signs that this email is a scam' items describing the image are kept as printed, so no key content is image-only. The scam-tactics list, the three MFA credential categories and the reporting destinations are kept as • items; the numbered 'Four Ways To Protect Yourself From Phishing' list keeps its 1.–4. numbering. Inline links flattened to their text (IdentityTheft.gov, ReportFraud.ftc.gov, reportphishing@apwg.org, 'SPAM (7726)'). Curly quotes kept as served. Whitespace normalised.
purpose: library: phishing recognition and response — common scam tactics (a story to trick you, fake suspicious-activity claims, account problems, unrecognized invoices, payment links with malware, fake government refunds, coupons), a worked example spotting a fake email by its three signs, the numbered four-step protection process (security software, automatic updates, multi-factor authentication, backups), the three MFA credential categories (something you know / something you have / something you are), the do-I-have-an-account decision question with its No/Yes branches, what to do after responding, and the three reporting destinations. Fits step ordering, a compare table of MFA credential types, and quiz cards.
